traits: Cap 3 to 12 cm, olive-brown to grey or sooty-brown, slimy, with dark streaks and a persistent dark boss
Gills thick, widely spaced, white, waxy
Stem 3 to 12 cm, slimy when wet, white above a ring-like zone, with ragged dark scaly bands below
Thin white flesh, no distinct smell, bland taste
Under conifers, in mountain woods, on acid ground · late summer to early winter
safetyNote: Edible, with divided opinions on taste: the DGfM lists it; Wikipedia (en) says some remove the cap skin, advises caution, and that it is eaten more in Europe than in North America. The page says there is no risk of confusion with toxic fungi, and lists other waxy caps as look-alikes (Hygrophorus latitabundus, H. pustulatus, H. persoonii under oaks). It has no French Wikipedia page: the text comes from Wikipedia (en) and the DGfM.

sources.title: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Mykologie (DGfM), Fachausschuss Pilzverwertung und Toxikologie (2026). Positivliste der Speisepilze, Stand 1. Mai 2026.
